rationale.conceptual: Requires implementing a phase-field model using finite elements in a non-trivial geometry with adaptive meshing, but the underlying physics and numerical method are well-established (Landau mean-field theory, conjugate gradient minimization). rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline: validate flat interface, run FEM minimizations for many (radius, separation) pairs, post-process free energy, interpolate binodal, compute forces via finite differences. Requires integrating an adaptive-mesh FE library (FEniCS/scikit-fem), handling boundary conditions, and ensuring sufficient resolution to capture the first-order jump.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies a standard phase-field mean-field model to study capillary bridging in sphere-plane geometry. Implementing the method requires setting up and solving a variational problem with finite elements and adaptive meshing, then post-processing to extract free energy, binodal, and force curves. The physics is well-established but the numerical implementation in a non-trivial geometry is moderate. The pipeline is multi-stage and involves careful tool integration, making execution moderately high.
